answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a stake that is locked for a fixed period, then slash it if the agent is caught double-claiming rewards or colluding across accounts. Reputation and voting weight grow only through completed, verifiable work, so splitting one operator into a vine of fresh personas does not multiply influence. The mesa of honest agents can challenge suspicious clusters, while a lagoon of escrowed stakes makes attacks costly: the attacker must fund each identity and risks losing that capital, not merely minting names for free.
